q: Two days after reporting an unshored trench to OSHA, a laborer is moved to night shifts at lower pay. To pursue a Section 11(c) retaliation claim, he must file a complaint with OSHA within:
why: Section 11(c) of the OSH Act gives employees 30 days from the retaliatory action to file; other whistleblower laws OSHA enforces have different deadlines.

q: A contractor makes its employment tax deposit 9 calendar days after the due date. What failure-to-deposit penalty rate applies to the late amount?
why: Deposits 1-5 days late draw 2%, 6-15 days late 5%, more than 15 days late 10%, and amounts still unpaid more than 10 days after the first IRS notice 15%.

q: A contractor's CGL policy (no endorsements) has a $500 per-occurrence deductible. One crane accident causes $4,200 in injuries to two of the contractor's laborers, $3,600 damage to a neighbor's parked car, $2,900 damage to scaffolding the contractor owns and $1,800 loss of lumber the contractor bought for the job. How much does the CGL insurer pay?
ref: ISO CG 00 01 exclusions e and j
why: CGL covers only third-party injury or damage, so only the $3,600 car claim counts, less the $500 deductible. Employee injuries go to workers' comp, and the contractor's own scaffolding and lumber are excluded owned property.

q: A contractor's workers' compensation rates are $0.15 per $100 of clerical payroll and $4.00 per $100 of carpentry payroll. Annual payroll is $40,000 clerical and $150,000 carpentry, and the insurer gives a 10% credit for a written safety program. What is the annual premium?
why: Clerical: 400 x $0.15 = $60; carpentry: 1,500 x $4.00 = $6,000; total $6,060 less the 10% credit = $5,454. Rates apply per $100 of payroll in each class.

q: A non-exempt carpenter paid $22.00 per hour works 47 hours in one workweek. What is the overtime premium portion of his pay?
why: The premium is the extra half-time on hours over 40: 7 hours x $11.00 = $77. His total gross pay would be 47 x $22 + $77 = $1,111.

q: In a CPM schedule an activity has an early start of day 12, a late start of day 15, an early finish of day 20 and a late finish of day 23. How much total float does it have?
why: Total float is late finish minus early finish (23 - 20) or late start minus early start (15 - 12): 3 days the activity can slip without delaying project completion.

q: A three-member general partnership made a profit last year. Which federal return must the partnership itself file to report its income and each partner's share?
why: A partnership pays no federal income tax but must file the Form 1065 information return every year and issue each partner a Schedule K-1. Form 1120 is for C corporations, 1120-S for S corporations and Schedule C for sole proprietors.

q: A sole proprietor owes self-employment tax once net earnings from self-employment for the year reach at least:
why: Self-employment tax (15.3% for Social Security and Medicare) applies when net self-employment earnings are $400 or more; it is figured on Schedule SE and filed with Form 1040.

q: A subcontract clause excuses late completion caused by events beyond either party's control, such as a regional trade strike or a hurricane. This is a:
why: A force majeure clause shields a party from liability for delay caused by events it cannot control, usually by granting extra time. A liquidated damages clause does the opposite, charging a set amount per day of late completion.

q: What is the maximum number of shareholders an S corporation may have?
why: An S corporation is limited to 100 shareholders (family members may count as one) and one class of stock; a C corporation has no shareholder limit.

q: A new hire wants to present only one document for Form I-9. Which one is acceptable by itself to prove both identity and employment authorization?
why: A U.S. passport or passport card is a List A document. A state ID or voter registration card is List B (identity only) and a birth certificate is List C (work authorization only), so each must be paired with a document from the other list.

q: Under the 2021 IMC, the minimum clear attic access opening for an attic containing an appliance is:
why: The attic opening must be at least 20 x 30 inches and large enough to remove the largest appliance.

q: What is the maximum length of a standard attic passageway (30 in high x 22 in wide) from the opening to the appliance?
why: The standard passageway is limited to 20 ft; 50 ft is allowed only if it is at least 6 ft high and 22 in wide.

q: An attic passageway that is unobstructed and at least 6 ft high and 22 in wide may be up to how long?
why: The attic exception extends the passageway limit to 50 ft when it is at least 6 ft high and 22 in wide.

q: The continuous solid flooring in an attic passageway to an appliance must be at least how wide?
why: The passageway needs continuous solid flooring at least 24 inches wide.

q: Where must the switch for the required attic appliance light be located?
why: A luminaire controlled by a switch at the passageway opening is required, plus a receptacle near the appliance.

q: The minimum access opening to an appliance located in a crawl space under a floor is:
why: Under-floor appliance access openings must be at least 22 x 30 inches.

q: A room containing appliances (outside a dwelling unit) must have a door and passageway at least:
why: Appliance rooms need a door and unobstructed passageway at least 36 in wide and 80 in high.

q: What level working space is required in front of the control side of an appliance?
why: A level working space at least 30 in deep and 30 in wide is required at the control side.

q: A permanent means of access to rooftop equipment is required when a person would have to climb more than how high above grade?
why: Permanent access is required where climbing more than 16 ft above grade would be needed.

q: On a roof with a slope of 3:12 or more and an edge more than 30 in above grade, serviceable equipment needs a level platform of at least:
why: A level platform at least 30 inches in every dimension, with guards, is required on each service side.

q: Guards are required when rooftop equipment needing service is within what distance of a roof edge that is more than 30 in above the surface below?
why: Equipment or roof hatches within 10 ft of such an edge require guards.

q: Rooftop equipment guards must have a top at least how high above the adjacent surface?
why: Guards must be at least 42 inches high and extend 30 inches beyond each end of the equipment.

q: In a residential garage, a gas furnace that is NOT listed as flammable-vapor-ignition-resistant (FVIR) must have its ignition source at least how high above the floor?
why: Ignition sources in garages must be at least 18 inches above the floor; appliances listed as FVIR (such as most modern gas water heaters) are exempt from this elevation requirement.

q: Unless protected from vehicle impact, appliances in a private garage must have a minimum clearance above the floor of:
why: Private garage appliances need 6 ft of clearance above the floor unless protected from impact.

q: In a public or repair garage, appliances must be installed at least how high above the floor (unless protected from impact)?
why: Public garage appliances must be at least 8 ft above the floor.

q: A condensing unit set on a pad at grade must be supported at least how far above the adjoining grade?
why: At-grade equipment sits on a slab at least 3 in above grade or is suspended at least 6 in above grade.

q: Which is a permitted location for a fuel-fired appliance under the prohibited-location rule?
c: A storage closet, natural draft furnace
A bedroom, natural draft water heater
A toilet room, Category I furnace
why: Direct-vent appliances are an exception to the prohibition on sleeping rooms, bathrooms, toilet rooms and storage closets.

q: The NEC requires a 125-V service receptacle within what distance of rooftop HVAC equipment?
why: A 15- or 20-A, 125-V receptacle is required within 25 ft of HVAC equipment on the same level.

q: Required heating systems must be able to maintain what indoor temperature 3 ft above the floor on the design heating day?
why: The IMC requires capacity to maintain at least 68 F at 3 ft above the floor.

q: What is the minimum internal diameter of a condensate drain line from a single cooling coil?
why: Condensate drains must be at least 3/4 in ID and may not decrease in size.

q: Condensate drains from units totaling 30 tons are manifolded together. The minimum common drain size is:
why: Over 20 to 40 tons requires a 1-inch condensate line.

q: Manifolded condensate drains serving 100 tons of equipment require a minimum pipe size of:
why: Over 90 to 125 tons requires 1-1/2 inch pipe.

q: An auxiliary drain pan under an attic air handler must be at least how deep?
why: Auxiliary pans must be at least 1-1/2 inches deep.

q: An auxiliary drain pan must be larger than the unit or coil by at least:
why: The pan must be at least 3 inches larger than the unit or coil in width and length.

q: A galvanized steel auxiliary drain pan must be at least what thickness?
why: Galvanized auxiliary pans must be at least 0.0236 in (No. 24 gage).

q: Water-level detection devices used to shut off equipment when a condensate drain clogs must conform to:
why: Water-level shutoff devices must conform to UL 508.

q: On a down-flow unit with no room for a secondary pan, where must the water-level monitoring device be installed?
c: In the drain line outside the unit
why: For down-flow units, the device goes inside the primary drain pan; external or in-line devices are not allowed.

q: Condensate drains for ductless mini-split equipment must have:
c: An inline check valve or a trap
why: Mini-split condensate drains need an inline check valve or a trap.

q: Natural ventilation of a space requires openable exterior openings of at least what percent of the floor area?
why: The minimum openable area to the outdoors is 4 percent of the floor area.

q: Using Vbz = Rp x Pz + Ra x Az, what outdoor air is required for a 1,000 sq ft office with 5 people (Rp = 5 cfm, Ra = 0.06 cfm/sq ft)?
A dwelling bathroom exhaust fan that runs intermittently must provide at least:
why: Bathrooms require 50 cfm intermittent or 20 cfm continuous.

q: A dwelling kitchen exhaust that runs intermittently must provide at least:
why: Kitchens require 100 cfm intermittent or 25 cfm continuous.

q: Using 0.01 x floor area + 7.5 x (bedrooms + 1), the continuous whole-house ventilation for a 2,000 sq ft, 3-bedroom home is:
Under the 2021 IRC, whole-house mechanical ventilation is required when a dwelling's blower door test result is at or below:
why: IRC 2021 R303.4 requires whole-house mechanical ventilation where tested air leakage is 5 air changes per hour or less at 50 Pa (earlier editions said less than 5).

q: A mechanical outdoor-air intake must be at least how far horizontally from a hazardous or noxious contaminant source such as a plumbing vent?
why: Intakes must be at least 10 ft horizontally from contaminant sources.

q: In a public toilet room with an intermittently operated exhaust fan, the exhaust rate per water closet or urinal is:
why: Public toilet rooms need 70 cfm per fixture intermittent or 50 cfm continuous.

q: A residential bath exhaust outlet must terminate at least how far from a mechanical air intake (unless 3 ft above it)?
why: Exhaust openings need 10 ft from mechanical intakes, or 3 ft vertical separation above them.

q: Environmental air exhaust (such as toilet exhaust) must terminate at least how far from property lines?
why: Environmental exhaust must be 3 ft from property lines and operable openings, and 10 ft from mechanical intakes.

q: Which is an acceptable termination for a bathroom exhaust fan?
c: Into the attic near a gable vent
why: Exhaust must discharge directly outdoors, not into attics, soffits, ridge vents or crawl spaces.

q: The maximum developed length of a domestic dryer exhaust duct, before fitting deductions, is:
why: The limit is 35 ft from the transition duct connection to the outlet, reduced for fittings.

q: How much must be deducted from the dryer duct length for each 4-in-radius mitered 90-degree elbow?
why: A 4-in-radius mitered 90-degree elbow counts as 5 ft of duct.

q: A dryer duct has two 4-in-radius mitered 90s and one mitered 45. What is the maximum straight duct allowed?
The dryer transition duct must be listed to UL 2158A and may be no longer than:
why: Transition ducts are limited to a single length of 8 ft and may not be concealed.

q: When a dryer duct's equivalent length exceeds 35 ft, a label stating the length must be placed within what distance of the duct connection?
why: The permanent label or tag goes within 6 ft of the exhaust duct connection.

q: Screws used at dryer exhaust duct joints may protrude into the duct no more than:
why: Fasteners may not protrude more than 1/8 inch into the duct, to limit lint buildup.

q: Dryer exhaust must terminate at least how far from openings into the building (absent other manufacturer instructions)?
why: Dryer terminations must be at least 3 ft from openings, and screens are not allowed.

q: Under IRC M1503.6, where a natural-draft fuel-burning appliance is located inside the dwelling's air barrier, a range hood requires makeup air when it can exhaust more than:
why: Exhaust systems over 400 cfm need makeup air at about the exhaust rate through an automatically opening damper, but only where a fuel-burning appliance that is neither direct-vent nor mechanical-draft is inside the air barrier.

q: The minimum slope for a horizontal grease duct 50 ft long serving a Type I hood is:
why: Horizontal grease ducts slope at least 1/4 in per ft; runs over 75 ft need 1 in per ft.

q: Grease duct systems serving Type I hoods must maintain a minimum air velocity of:
why: The minimum grease duct velocity is 500 feet per minute.

q: A steel grease duct must be at least what thickness?
why: Grease ducts must be 16 gage steel or 18 gage stainless steel.

q: Without a listed reduction, a grease duct needs what clearance to combustible construction?
why: Grease ducts need 18 in to combustibles and 3 in to noncombustibles.

q: A canopy-type commercial kitchen hood must overhang the cooking appliances on open sides by at least:
why: Canopy hoods must extend at least 6 inches beyond the appliances on all open sides.

q: The lowest edge of grease filters above an exposed charcoal or charbroil fire must be at least:
why: Filters must be 3.5 ft above charcoal/charbroil fires, 2 ft above exposed flame, 0.5 ft otherwise.

q: A rooftop grease exhaust outlet must discharge at least how high above the roof surface?
why: Rooftop grease duct terminations discharge at least 40 inches above the roof.

q: Flexible air connectors are limited in length to:
why: Flexible air connectors may be no longer than 14 ft and may not pass through walls, floors or ceilings.

q: Gypsum board may be used to form air ducts only when:
c: It carries supply air under 140 F
It carries return air not over 125 F
why: Gypsum shafts are limited to return air at 125 F or less, with surfaces above dew point.

q: Duct coverings and linings must have a maximum flame spread index of 25 and a maximum smoke-developed index of:
why: Coverings and linings are limited to flame spread 25 and smoke-developed 50.

q: Tape listed for sealing flexible air ducts carries which marking?
why: UL 181B covers flex duct closures; tapes are marked 181B-FX and mastics 181B-M.

q: A stud wall cavity used as a plenum in a building may carry:
why: Stud cavity and joist space plenums are limited to return air and may not serve more than one floor level.

q: Duct smoke detectors are required in the return air of systems with a design capacity greater than:
why: Return air smoke detection is required above 2,000 cfm, upstream of filters and outdoor air connections.

q: A fire damper installed in a 2-hour fire-resistance-rated wall must have a minimum rating of:
why: Assemblies rated less than 3 hours need 1-1/2-hour fire dampers.

q: Fire damper access points must be labeled with letters at least how tall?
why: Labels reading FIRE DAMPER, SMOKE DAMPER or FIRE/SMOKE DAMPER must have letters at least 1/2 inch high.

q: Ducts penetrating the wall between a house and its attached garage must be at least:
c: No. 30 gage steel with no openings
No. 26 gage steel with no openings into the garage
No. 22 gage steel with a fire damper
why: Garage ducts and penetrating ducts must be at least 26 gage steel and have no openings into the garage.

q: Under the 2021 IECC, a 6-inch supply duct in a vented attic must be insulated to at least:
why: Ducts 3 in and larger outside conditioned space need R-8.

q: What is the maximum total duct leakage for a 2,000 sq ft home tested post-construction under the 2021 IECC?
why: 4.0 cfm per 100 sq ft x 20 = 80 cfm at 25 Pa.

q: Using the standard method, how much room volume is needed for appliances totaling 140,000 Btu/h to use indoor combustion air?
why: 50 cu ft per 1,000 Btu/h x 140 = 7,000 cu ft.

q: Two indoor openings connecting rooms on the same story for combustion air must each be at least:
c: 1 sq in per 1,000 Btu/h, minimum 100 sq in
why: Each opening needs 1 sq in per 1,000 Btu/h of total input, but not less than 100 sq in.

q: Two outdoor combustion air openings connected through horizontal ducts must each provide:
why: Horizontal ducts require 1 sq in per 2,000 Btu/h; direct or vertical ducts 1 per 4,000.

q: A 120,000 Btu/h appliance uses two outdoor openings through vertical ducts. Each opening must have a free area of at least:
why: 120,000 / 4,000 = 30 sq in per opening.

q: A single permanent outdoor combustion air opening must provide at least:
why: One opening needs 1 sq in per 3,000 Btu/h, located within 12 in of the top.

q: Mechanical combustion air systems must supply at least:
why: Mechanical combustion air must be at least 0.35 cfm per 1,000 Btu/h, interlocked with the appliance.

q: When louver free area is unknown, metal louvers are assumed to have a free area of:
why: Metal louvers are assumed 75 percent free area; wood louvers 25 percent.

q: A condensing furnace whose vent operates under positive pressure is classified as Category:
why: Category IV appliances have positive vent pressure and produce condensate.

q: Vent connectors must slope upward toward the vent or chimney at a minimum of:
why: Connectors must rise at least 1/4 inch per foot with no dips or sags.

q: With a 20 ft high gas vent, the maximum horizontal length of a single-wall connector is:
why: Single-wall connectors are limited to 75 percent of vent height: 0.75 x 20 = 15 ft.

q: A single-wall connector from a listed draft-hood appliance needs what clearance to combustibles?
why: Single-wall connectors on listed draft-hood appliances need 6 inches unless the listing says otherwise.

q: A chimney serving residential-type or low-heat appliances must extend at least 3 ft above the roof penetration and at least how far above any part of the building within 10 ft?
why: This is the 3-2-10 rule: 3 ft above the roof, 2 ft above anything within 10 ft.

q: A Type B gas vent must terminate at least how far above the highest connected draft hood or flue collar?
why: Type B and L vents need 5 ft of vertical height; B-W vents need 12 ft.

q: A mechanical draft vent terminal must be at least how far above any door, operable window or gravity air inlet (if not 4 ft below or beside it)?
why: Power vent terminals must be 4 ft below, 4 ft horizontally from, or 1 ft above such openings.

q: A direct-vent appliance rated 40,000 Btu/h needs what minimum terminal clearance from an air opening into the building?
why: Over 10,000 to 50,000 Btu/h requires 9 inches.

q: Gas piping must be tested at 1-1/2 times the maximum working pressure, but never less than:
why: The minimum gas test pressure is 3 psig regardless of design pressure.

q: What is the minimum duration of a gas piping pressure test?
why: The test must last at least 10 minutes.

q: Which test medium is prohibited for gas piping tests?
why: Oxygen may never be used; air, nitrogen, CO2 or inert gas are allowed.

q: An appliance gas shutoff valve must be in the same room and within what distance of the appliance?
why: Shutoff valves must be accessible, in the same room and within 6 ft.

q: The maximum overall length of a flexible gas appliance connector is:
why: Connectors are limited to 6 ft, one per appliance, and may not pass through walls or floors.

q: Which appliance is exempt from the sediment trap requirement?
why: Ranges, clothes dryers, illuminating appliances, decorative vented appliances and outdoor grills are exempt.

q: The bonding jumper for a CSST gas system must be at least:
why: CSST bonding jumpers must be 6 AWG copper or equivalent and no longer than 75 ft.

q: General underground gas piping must be buried at least how deep?
why: Underground gas piping needs 12 in of cover; individual lines to outdoor grills or lights may be 8 in.

q: Gas piping bored through a stud less than 1-1/2 in from its face requires a steel shield plate at least:
why: Shield plates must be at least No. 16 gage and extend 4 in beyond the member.

q: Horizontal 1/2-inch steel gas pipe must be supported at intervals of no more than:
why: 1/2-in steel pipe is supported every 6 ft; 3/4 and 1 in every 8 ft; 1-1/4 in and larger every 10 ft.

q: Which statement about propane is correct?
c: It has about 1,000 Btu per cubic foot
It is heavier than air and collects in low areas
It is tabulated in CFH in IFGC sizing tables
why: Propane has a specific gravity near 1.5, so it sinks and collects in low spots.

q: Using about 1,000 Btu per cubic foot, how much natural gas does a 100,000 Btu/h furnace need?
why: 100,000 / 1,000 = 100 cubic feet per hour.

q: Hydronic piping must be hydrostatically tested at 1-1/2 times design pressure, but not less than:
why: Hydronic tests are at 1.5 x design pressure, minimum 100 psi, held at least 15 minutes.

q: A 10 GPM hydronic loop with a 20 F temperature drop delivers about:
ref: Q = 500 x GPM x delta T

q: How much pressure does a 25 ft column of water exert at its base?
why: 25 x 0.433 = about 10.8 psi.

q: What control is required on steam and hot water boilers to shut down the burner if water drops too low?
why: Boilers need a low-water cutoff (forced-circulation coil boilers may use a flow switch).

q: An ASME Section IV low-pressure steam boiler operates at no more than:
why: Low-pressure steam heating boilers are limited to 15 psi; hot water boilers to 160 psi and 250 F.

q: R-454B and R-32 are classified in which ASHRAE 34 safety group?
why: Both are lower-toxicity, lower-flammability (2L) refrigerants.

q: In a refrigerant safety classification such as B1, the letter B indicates:
why: A = lower toxicity, B = higher toxicity; the number shows flammability.

q: Machinery room emergency ventilation is Q = 100 x the square root of G. For a system holding 100 lb, Q is:
why: 100 x square root of 100 = 100 x 10 = 1,000 cfm.

q: Outdoor refrigerant access ports must be fitted with:
why: Outdoor access ports need locking, tamper-resistant caps or other security.

q: Which gas may be used to pressure test field-erected refrigerant piping?
why: Use dry nitrogen or another inert gas; oxygen, air and combustible gases are prohibited.

q: Under EPA's Technology Transitions rule, new residential split AC systems manufactured from January 1, 2025 must use refrigerant with a GWP below:
why: The limit for residential and light commercial AC and heat pumps is GWP below 700.

q: Under 40 CFR 82.157, the leak rate that triggers repair for a comfort cooling appliance with 50 lb or more of R-22 is:
why: Comfort cooling is 10 percent; commercial refrigeration 20; industrial process 30.

q: The leak rate threshold for commercial refrigeration appliances with 50 lb or more is:
why: Commercial refrigeration (retail food and cold storage) triggers repair at 20 percent per year.

q: After a comfort cooling appliance exceeds its leak rate, leaks must normally be repaired within:
why: Repairs are due within 30 days, or 120 days if an industrial process shutdown is needed.

q: A follow-up verification test must be done within how many days of a successful initial verification test?
why: The follow-up verification test is due within 10 days.

q: Appliances that leak 125 percent or more of their full charge in a calendar year must be reported to EPA by:
why: Chronically leaking appliance reports are due March 1 of the following year.

q: Using the annualizing method, 10 lb added to a 100 lb system 73 days after the last addition gives a leak rate of:
why: 10/100 x 365/73 x 100 = 50 percent per year.

q: Before disposal, a high-pressure appliance with less than 200 lb of charge must be evacuated to:
why: High-pressure appliances under 200 lb require 0 inches of mercury.

q: Using recovery equipment made after November 15, 1993, a medium-pressure appliance with 200 lb or more must be evacuated to:
why: Medium-pressure 200 lb or more requires 15 in Hg; under 200 lb requires 10 in Hg.

q: Using recovery equipment made on or after November 15, 1993, the required evacuation level for a low-pressure (R-123) chiller is:
why: Low-pressure appliances must be evacuated to 25 mm Hg absolute with post-1993 recovery equipment (25 in Hg vacuum with older equipment).

q: Recovery equipment made after November 15, 1993 used on a small appliance with a running compressor must recover:
why: 90 percent with the compressor running, 80 percent if not, or evacuate to 4 in Hg.

q: System-dependent recovery equipment may not be used on appliances with a full charge of more than:
why: System-dependent equipment is limited to appliances with 15 lb or less.

q: Which of these is a major repair under EPA rules?
why: Removing the compressor, condenser, evaporator or auxiliary coil is a major repair.

q: Under EPA definitions, R-134a is used in what type of appliance?
why: R-134a and R-12 are medium-pressure refrigerants (45 to 170 psia at 104 F).

q: What is the passing score for a closed-book EPA 608 Type II exam?
why: Closed-book tests require 70 percent; Type I mail-in tests require 84 percent.

q: The passing score for a Type I EPA 608 test given in mail-in format is:
why: Mail-in Type I tests require 84 percent.

q: How many questions are on a Universal EPA 608 certification exam?
why: Universal is 100 questions: 25 Core plus 25 each for Types I, II and III.

q: How long is an EPA Section 608 technician certification valid?
why: Section 608 certification currently does not expire.

q: Since January 1, 2018, the EPA refrigerant sales restriction also applies to:
why: The sales restriction expanded to non-exempt substitutes like R-410A and R-134a.

q: Reclaimed refrigerant must meet the purity standard of:
why: Reclaimers process refrigerant to Appendix A purity, based on AHRI 700; AHRI 740 is for recovery equipment.

q: Before used refrigerant can be sold to a new owner for use as refrigerant, it must be:
why: Used refrigerant changing ownership must be reclaimed by a certified reclaimer.

q: Which refrigerant may be vented in a commercial or industrial process refrigeration system without violating Section 608?
why: Ammonia in commercial/industrial process refrigeration and absorption units is an exempt substitute.

q: A scrap recycler accepting a refrigerator without recovering the refrigerant itself must obtain a signed statement listing:
c: The recoverer's name and address and the recovery date
The technician's certification card number only
why: The statement must give the name and address of the person who recovered the refrigerant and the date.

q: Refillable recovery cylinders are identified by which colors?
why: Recovery cylinders are gray with a yellow top (shoulder).

q: How often must refillable DOT recovery cylinders be hydrostatically retested?
why: Recovery cylinders are retested every 5 years and stamped with the test date.

q: Starting January 1, 2026, EPA's HFC leak repair requirements apply to appliances with at least how much refrigerant?
why: The ER&R rule covers appliances with 15 lb or more of HFC with GWP above 53.

q: A low-pressure chiller's rupture disc is typically set at 15 psig, so leak-test pressure should not exceed:
why: Raise pressure no higher than 10 psig to stay below the rupture disc setting.

q: In what state does refrigerant leave the compressor?
why: The compressor discharges high-pressure, high-temperature superheated vapor.

q: The condenser saturation temperature is 110 F and the liquid line is 100 F. What is the subcooling?
why: Subcooling = 110 - 100 = 10 F.

q: In a TXV, which pressure acts to open the valve?
why: Bulb pressure opens the valve; evaporator and spring pressure close it.

q: High superheat combined with low subcooling most likely indicates:
why: Both readings point to an undercharged system.

q: At 100 percent relative humidity, how do dry-bulb, wet-bulb and dew point compare?
why: Saturated air has equal dry-bulb, wet-bulb and dew point temperatures.

q: How many grains of moisture equal one pound of water?
why: There are 7,000 grains in a pound.

q: A system removes 18,000 Btu/h sensible out of 24,000 Btu/h total. What is the sensible heat ratio?
Using Q = 0.68 x CFM x delta grains, what latent load is removed by 1,000 CFM with a 20-grain drop?
ref: Q = 0.68 x CFM x delta grains

q: Using Q = 4.5 x CFM x delta h, what is the total load for 1,000 CFM with an enthalpy change of 6 Btu/lb?
ref: Q = 4.5 x CFM x delta h

q: About how much airflow does a 3.5-ton air conditioner need at 400 CFM per ton?
800 CFM flows through a 12 in x 8 in duct. What is the air velocity?
A fan's speed is increased from 1,000 to 1,200 RPM. Its static pressure changes by a factor of:
why: Static pressure varies with speed squared: 1.2 squared = 1.44.

q: If fan speed increases by 20 percent, the brake horsepower increases by a factor of about:
why: Horsepower varies with speed cubed: 1.2 cubed = 1.728.

q: A 10 kW electric heat strip produces approximately:
Supply static is +0.30 in w.c. and return static is -0.20 in w.c. What is the total external static pressure?
why: Add the magnitudes: 0.30 + 0.20 = 0.50 in w.c.

q: Discharge is 250 psig and suction is 70 psig. What is the compression ratio?
On an HVAC nameplate, which value sets the largest breaker or fuse permitted?
why: MOCP is the maximum overcurrent protection; MCA sizes the conductors.

q: Under the NEC, 'within sight' of AC equipment means visible and no more than:
why: A disconnect within sight must be visible and not more than 50 ft away.

q: Which thermostat terminal normally energizes the condensing unit contactor?
why: Y calls for cooling and energizes the compressor contactor; G runs the indoor fan.

q: What is the DOE 2023 minimum efficiency for a 3-ton split air conditioner installed in Tennessee (Southeast region)?
why: In the Southeast, split AC under 45,000 Btu/h needs 14.3 SEER2.

q: The national 2023 minimum for a split-system heat pump is 14.3 SEER2 and:
why: Split heat pumps require 14.3 SEER2 and 7.5 HSPF2.

q: A 36,000 Btu/h air conditioner draws 3,000 W at rated conditions. Its EER is:
What indoor design temperatures does the IECC set for residential load calculations?
why: Interior design conditions are 72 F for heating and 75 F for cooling.

q: Under the IPC, a DWV rough-in water test requires at least what head of water, held for how long?
why: The DWV water test uses at least a 10 ft head held for at least 15 minutes.

q: What pressure is used for an IPC DWV air test?
why: The air test is 5 psi or enough to balance a 10 in mercury column, held 15 minutes.

q: Under the IPC, which piping may NOT be tested with air?
why: The IPC prohibits air testing of plastic piping.

q: An air test of a non-plastic water supply system must be at least:
why: Water supply systems are tested at working pressure with water, or at 50 psi with air for non-plastic pipe, for 15 minutes.

q: A forced (pumped) sewer is tested at what pressure?
c: 5 psi greater than the pump rating
why: Forced sewers are tested at least 5 psi above the pump rating for 15 minutes.

q: How deep must water be at the threshold when testing a site-built shower liner?
why: The liner is filled to at least 2 in deep at the threshold and held 15 minutes.

q: How often must testable backflow assemblies such as RPZs be tested after installation?
why: They are tested at installation, after repair or relocation, and at least once a year.

q: Under the IPC, when a smoke test is used for the final DWV test, what pressure must be held for 15 minutes after the stack openings are closed?
why: The final test is visual; where a smoke test is used, a pressure equal to a 1 in water column is held for at least 15 minutes after smoke appears and the stack openings are closed.

q: Maximum horizontal hanger spacing for 1/2 in PEX tubing is:
why: PEX 1 in and smaller is supported every 32 in (2.67 ft) horizontally.

q: Copper tubing 1 in in diameter must be supported horizontally at least every:
why: Copper tubing 1-1/4 in and smaller is supported every 6 ft horizontally.

q: Hubless cast-iron pipe in 5 ft lengths needs horizontal support at least every:
why: Cast iron is supported every 5 ft (10 ft only where 10 ft lengths are installed).

q: Sway bracing is required at changes in direction greater than 45 degrees for pipe sizes of:
why: Rigid sway bracing is required for 4 in and larger pipe at changes over 45 degrees.

q: A sleeve for a pipe through a foundation wall must be how much larger than the pipe?
why: The sleeve must be two pipe sizes larger than the pipe passing through it.

q: Steel shield plates protecting concealed pipe must be at least what thickness?
why: Shield plates are at least 0.0575 in (No. 16 gauge) steel where pipe is within 1-1/2 in of the framing edge.

q: Trench backfill is placed and tamped in layers of what thickness until the pipe crown is covered by 12 in?
why: Loose earth is placed in 6 in layers and tamped until 12 in of tamped earth covers the crown.

q: Under the UPC, an earth tunnel for pipe installation is limited in length to one-half the trench depth, with a maximum of:
why: UPC tunnels need 2 ft of clear height above the pipe and are limited to half the trench depth, 8 ft maximum. The IPC sets no tunnel dimensions.

q: A trench parallel to a footing may not extend into the bearing plane, a line projected downward from the footing's outside bottom edge at:
why: The bearing plane slopes down at 45 degrees from the outside bottom edge of the footing.

q: Exterior water supply piping must be installed at least how far below the frost line?
why: It must be at least 6 in below the frost line and at least 12 in below grade.

q: Under the IPC, the building drain extends to what point outside the building wall, where the building sewer begins?
why: The building drain ends 30 in outside the exterior wall.

q: Under the IPC, a branch interval is a vertical distance between horizontal branch connections to a drainage stack of at least:
why: A branch interval is 8 ft or more in developed length between horizontal branch connections, measured down from the highest branch.

q: Under the IPC, a pipe installed at 30 degrees from horizontal is classified as:
why: Pipe at less than 45 degrees from horizontal is horizontal.

q: What is the temperature range of tempered water?
why: The IPC defines tempered water as 85 F to 110 F.

q: A capped branch is considered a dead end when its developed length is at least:
why: A dead end is a closed branch 2 ft or more in developed length.

q: Which of these is gray water under the IPC?
why: Gray water comes from lavatories, bathtubs, showers, clothes washers and laundry trays.

q: Minimum clearance from the center of a water closet to a side wall under the IPC:
why: Water closets must be at least 15 in from center to any side wall or obstruction.

q: Minimum clear space in front of a water closet under the IPC:
why: The IPC requires 21 in in front. The UPC requires 24 in.

q: Minimum size of a water closet compartment for a floor-mounted water closet:
why: Floor-mounted: 30 x 60 in. Wall-hung: 30 x 56 in.

q: Minimum interior area of a shower compartment under the IPC:
why: IPC showers need 900 sq in with a 30 in minimum dimension.

q: A shower with a 25 in minimum dimension is allowed under the IPC only if its area is at least:
why: The exception allows a 25 in minimum dimension with at least 1,300 sq in.

q: A site-built shower liner must turn up at least how far above the finished threshold?
why: Liners turn up at least 2 in above the threshold and slope 1/4 in per ft to the drain.

q: Minimum thickness of a PVC sheet shower liner:
why: PVC and CPE liners must be at least 0.040 in (40 mil).

q: In an assembly or educational occupancy, urinals may be substituted for up to what percentage of required water closets?
why: Up to 67% in assembly and educational occupancies; 50% in others.

q: The maximum hot water temperature an individual shower valve may be set to deliver is:
why: The installer sets the limit stop so outlet water does not exceed 120 F.

q: Maximum water temperature supplied to a bidet:
why: Bidet water is limited to 110 F by an ASSE 1070 device.

q: Minimum waste outlet diameter for a lavatory:
why: Lavatory waste outlets must be at least 1-1/4 in.

q: Minimum outlet size for a floor drain:
why: Floor drains need at least a 2 in outlet.

q: A fixture with concealed slip joints needs an access opening at least how large in its smallest dimension?
why: The access panel or utility space must be at least 12 in in its smallest dimension.

q: Maximum flow rate for a showerhead under the IPC:
why: Showerheads are limited to 2.5 gpm at 80 psi.

q: Separate men's and women's facilities are not required in a building whose total occupant load is no more than:
why: Separate facilities aren't required where the total occupant load is 15 or fewer.

q: Mercantile water closet ratio in Table 403.1:
why: Mercantile needs 1 water closet per 500 occupants.

q: Maximum path of travel to required toilet facilities (outside malls):
why: Travel distance may not exceed 500 ft (300 ft in malls).

q: An ADA water closet centerline must be how far from the side wall?
why: The accessible water closet centerline is 16 in minimum to 18 in maximum from the side wall.

q: Accessible water closet seat height (to top of seat):
why: Seat height is 17 in to 19 in above the floor.

q: Grab bars must be mounted at what height to the top of the gripping surface?
why: Grab bars are mounted 33 in to 36 in above the floor.

q: Maximum rim height of an accessible lavatory:
why: The rim or counter surface may be no higher than 34 in.

q: A water heater relief valve may be set no higher than the heater's rated working pressure or:
why: The relief valve setting is limited to the rated working pressure or 150 psi, whichever is less.

q: The temperature relief valve's sensing element must be in what part of the tank?
why: The valve must respond to water in the top 6 in of the tank.

q: Minimum depth of a water heater drain pan:
why: Pans must be at least 1-1/2 in deep with a 3/4 in drain.

q: Minimum diameter of a water heater pan drain:
why: The pan drain is an indirect waste pipe at least 3/4 in in diameter.

q: A pan drain run to the outdoors must end how far above the adjacent ground?
why: Outdoor pan drains terminate 6 in to 24 in above grade.

q: In a garage, a water heater's ignition source must be elevated at least:
why: Ignition sources must be at least 18 in above the garage floor unless the heater is FVIR-listed.

q: Which item is prohibited on water heater relief valve discharge piping?
why: The discharge end may not be threaded; it also may not be trapped or have valves or tees.

q: Under the UPC, where must seismic water heater straps be located?
c: Top and bottom 6 in of the tank
Upper third and lower third, lower strap 4 in above controls
Upper half, 12 in below the top
why: UPC strapping is in the upper and lower thirds, with the lower strap at least 4 in above the controls.

q: Minimum size of a water service pipe under the IPC:
why: The water service must be at least 3/4 in.

q: Minimum separation between the water service and building sewer (no exceptions applied):
c: 5 ft of undisturbed or compacted earth
why: The water service and building sewer must be separated by at least 5 ft.

q: Minimum fixture supply pipe size for a lavatory:
why: A lavatory supply may be 3/8 in.

q: Minimum fixture supply size for a flush-valve water closet:
why: Flush-valve water closets need a 1 in supply.

q: A water-hammer arrestor must comply with which standard?
why: Water-hammer arrestors conform to ASSE 1010.

q: Maximum weighted-average lead content for pipe and fittings supplying drinking water:
why: Drinking water components must meet NSF 372 with no more than 0.25% weighted average lead.

q: Under the IPC, which material is approved for underground water service but NOT for water distribution inside a building?
why: PVC is a water service material only; it isn't listed for interior distribution.

q: A booster pump low-pressure cutoff must stop the pump when suction pressure drops to:
why: The low-pressure cutoff activates at 10 psi or less on the suction side.

q: Maximum developed length of hot water piping from the source to a fixture:
why: The IPC limits hot or tempered water piping to 50 ft from the source.

q: When is a thermal expansion control device required on a storage water heater?
c: On every water heater regardless of system
When the cold supply passes through a check valve, PRV or backflow preventer
why: A closed system created by a check valve, PRV or backflow preventer requires thermal expansion control.

q: Which standard covers master thermostatic mixing valves installed at the water heater?
why: Temperature-actuated mixing valves at the source comply with ASSE 1017.

q: Which device protects against both back pressure and backsiphonage for a high-hazard connection?
why: The RPZ handles back pressure and backsiphonage at high hazard.

q: Which backflow device may NOT have a shutoff valve installed downstream of it?
why: An AVB can't be under continuous pressure, so no downstream valves are allowed.

q: An atmospheric vacuum breaker's critical level must be at least how far above the flood level rim or highest outlet?
why: AVBs are installed with the critical level at least 6 in above the flood level rim.

q: What is the minimum air gap for a lavatory faucet (effective opening up to 1/2 in) away from a wall?
why: Lavatory air gap is 1 in away from walls, 1-1/2 in near a wall.

q: How high must a barometric loop rise?
why: A barometric loop must extend at least 35 ft high.

q: A lawn irrigation system that injects fertilizer must be protected by:
why: Where chemicals are introduced, an RPZ is required.

q: Downstream piping from a carbonated beverage dispenser's backflow device must not be:
why: CO2 forms carbonic acid that attacks copper; downstream piping must resist CO2.

q: One approved disinfection method is a chlorine solution of at least 50 ppm held for:
why: 50 ppm for 24 hours, or 200 ppm for 3 hours.

q: Minimum slope for an 8 in horizontal drain under the IPC:
why: Drains 8 in and larger may slope 1/16 in per ft.

q: Horizontal branches must connect to the base of a stack at least how far downstream?
why: Connections must be at least 10 stack diameters downstream.

q: A sanitary tee is permitted for which change of direction?
why: Sanitary tees are only for horizontal-to-vertical changes.

q: DFU value of a private 1.6 gpf water closet:
why: Private 1.6 gpf water closets are 3 DFU; public are 4.

q: DFU value of a bathroom group with a 1.6 gpf water closet:
why: A bathroom group is 5 DFU with a 1.6 gpf water closet and 6 DFU with a higher-flush one.

q: DFU value of a residential clothes washer under the IPC:
why: IPC: 2 DFU residential, 3 DFU commercial. The UPC rates a domestic washer at 3.

q: Continuous flow into a drainage system is converted at:
why: Each gpm of continuous flow counts as 2 DFU.

q: Maximum DFU on a 4 in building drain at 1/4 in per ft:
why: 4 in at 1/4 in per ft carries 216 DFU (180 at 1/8, 250 at 1/2).

q: Maximum DFU on a 2 in horizontal fixture branch:
why: A 2 in horizontal fixture branch carries 6 DFU.

q: For a fixture not listed in Table 709.1 that has a 2 in trap, the DFU value is:
why: Table 709.2 assigns 3 DFU to a 2 in trap or fixture drain.

q: Maximum spacing of cleanouts on horizontal drains inside a building:
why: Cleanouts are required at intervals of no more than 100 ft.

q: Where a drain run has several changes of direction over 45 degrees, one cleanout is required for each:
why: With multiple changes of direction, one cleanout per 40 ft of developed length.

q: Required rodding clearance in front of a cleanout on a 4 in pipe:
why: 18 in for 6 in and smaller pipe; 36 in for 8 in and larger.

q: Minimum cleanout size on a 6 in drain:
why: Cleanouts match pipe size up to 4 in; for larger pipe, at least 4 in.

q: Minimum dimensions of a sump pit (unless otherwise approved):
why: Sump pits are at least 18 in in diameter and 24 in deep.

q: A sewage ejector receiving water closet discharge must pass spherical solids up to:
why: Ejectors serving water closets handle 2 in solids; others handle 1 in.

q: Minimum capacity of a sewage pump with a 2 in discharge:
why: 2 in = 21 gpm, 2-1/2 in = 30 gpm, 3 in = 46 gpm.

q: A backwater valve is required for fixtures whose flood level rims are below the elevation of:
c: The next upstream public sewer manhole cover
why: Fixtures with flood level rims below the manhole cover of the next upstream public sewer manhole need backwater valve protection; fixtures above it may not discharge through the valve (except in existing buildings).

q: An indirect waste pipe must be trapped when its horizontal developed length exceeds:
why: Trap it when it exceeds 30 in horizontally or 54 in total developed length.

q: A clothes washer standpipe must extend above its trap weir at least 18 in but not more than:
why: IPC standpipes are 18 in to 42 in above the trap weir.

q: Water above what temperature may not be discharged directly into the drainage system?
why: Waste above 140 F must discharge to an indirect waste receptor.

q: Vent systems must keep trap seals from being exposed to a pressure differential greater than:
why: Trap seals may not see more than a 1 in water column pressure differential.

q: A vent stack is required for every drainage stack with how many branch intervals or more?
why: Drainage stacks with five or more branch intervals need a vent stack.

q: A dry vent must rise vertically to at least how far above the flood level rim of the highest fixture before running horizontally?
why: Dry vents rise at least 6 in above the flood level rim before going horizontal.

q: Minimum size of any vent pipe under the IPC:
why: Vents are at least half the drain diameter and never less than 1-1/4 in.

q: A vent with more than what developed length must be increased one pipe size?
why: Vents over 40 ft in developed length are increased one nominal size.

q: Maximum trap-to-vent distance for a 1-1/2 in trap under the IPC:
why: Table 909.1: 1-1/2 in trap = 6 ft at 1/4 in per ft.

q: A vent may not be installed within how many pipe diameters of the trap weir?
why: Crown venting within two pipe diameters of the weir is prohibited.

q: Maximum number of fixtures that may be circuit vented on one horizontal branch:
why: A circuit vent may serve up to eight fixtures.

q: Maximum slope of the vent section of a circuit-vented horizontal branch:
why: The circuit-vented section may slope no more than 1 unit in 12 (8%).

q: Maximum slope of a horizontal combination waste and vent pipe:
why: Combination waste and vent piping may slope no more than 1/2 in per ft.

q: A 2 in wet vent may carry a maximum of how many DFU?
why: Wet vent sizes: 1-1/2 in = 1, 2 in = 4, 2-1/2 in = 6, 3 in = 12 DFU.

q: Relief vents are required on soil and waste stacks having more than how many branch intervals?
why: Stacks over 10 branch intervals need relief vents at every tenth interval.

q: Individual and branch air admittance valves must be at least how far above the horizontal branch or fixture drain they vent?
why: Branch AAVs: 4 in above the drain. Stack AAVs: 6 in above the highest flood rim.

q: Individual and branch-type air admittance valves must comply with:
why: ASSE 1051 covers individual and branch AAVs; ASSE 1050 covers stack-type.

q: An open vent terminal within 10 ft horizontally of an operable window must be at least how far above the top of the window?
why: Within 10 ft horizontally, the vent must be at least 3 ft above the opening.

q: A sidewall vent terminal must be at least how far from a lot line?
why: Through-wall vents are at least 10 ft from the lot line and 10 ft above average grade.

q: Where a roof is used as a sun deck or promenade, vent pipes must extend at least how far above the roof?
why: Vents on occupied roofs terminate at least 7 ft above the roof.

q: Maximum vertical distance from a fixture outlet to the trap weir:
why: Vertical distance is 24 in max; horizontal distance is 30 in max.

q: Which trap is prohibited by the IPC?
why: S-traps, bell traps, drum traps, crown-vented traps and moving-part traps are prohibited.

q: One trap may serve a two-compartment sink if the compartments differ in depth by no more than:
why: Compartments may differ by up to 6 in, with outlets no more than 30 in apart.

q: An oil separator at a repair garage needs at least how much capacity for the first 100 sq ft drained?
why: 6 cu ft for the first 100 sq ft plus 1 cu ft per additional 100 sq ft.

q: Commercial laundry interceptors must stop solids of at least what size?
why: The basket must stop solids 1/2 in or larger.

q: Storm drainage is sized using which rainfall rate?
why: IPC storm sizing uses the 100-year hourly rainfall rate.

q: When a vertical wall drains onto a roof, what portion of the wall area is added to the roof area?
why: Add one-half the wall area to the projected roof area.

q: Under the UPC, each gpm of continuous flow into a storm drain is counted as how much roof area?
why: The UPC counts 1 gpm of continuous flow as 24 sq ft of roof area, based on a 4 in/hr rainfall rate (24 x 4 x 0.0104 = 1 gpm).

q: Minimum opening dimension of a secondary (overflow) scupper:
why: Scuppers may not have any opening dimension under 4 in.

q: Minimum diameter of a subsoil drain:
why: Subsoil drains must be at least 4 in in diameter.

q: Minimum test pressure for a fuel gas piping system:
c: 1-1/2 times working pressure, not less than 3 psig
2 times working pressure, not less than 5 psig
why: The test is at least 1.5 x working pressure and never below 3 psig.

q: Minimum gas pressure test duration for a single-family dwelling:
why: Single-family dwellings and systems under 10 cu ft: at least 10 minutes.

q: Minimum size of a CSST bonding conductor (copper):
why: The CSST bonding conductor must be at least 6 AWG copper, no longer than 75 ft.

q: Maximum length of a gas appliance connector:
why: Connectors may not exceed 6 ft, one per appliance.

q: Minimum burial depth for underground gas piping (general):
why: 12 in generally; 8 in for individual lines to outdoor appliances.

q: Minimum size of the tracer wire for underground plastic gas pipe:
why: A yellow insulated copper tracer at least 18 AWG is required.

q: Shield plates for gas piping must extend at least how far above sole plates and below top plates?
why: The IFGC requires 4 in, compared with 2 in in the IPC.

q: Support spacing for 1/2 in steel gas pipe:
why: 1/2 in steel: 6 ft; 3/4 to 1 in: 8 ft; 1-1/4 in and larger: 10 ft.

q: The standard method for indoor combustion air requires how much room volume?
why: The standard method requires 50 cu ft per 1,000 Btu/h of input.

q: With two openings directly to the outdoors, each opening needs a free area of at least:
why: Direct or vertical-duct openings need 1 sq in per 4,000 Btu/h each.

q: If the free area of a wood louver is unknown, assume:
why: Wood louvers are assumed 25% free area; metal louvers 75%.

q: OSHA requires a ladder or other exit in trenches of what depth?
why: Trenches 4 ft or deeper need egress within 25 ft of lateral travel.

q: Maximum lateral travel distance to a means of egress in a trench:
why: No more than 25 ft of lateral travel.

q: A protective system is required in excavations at least how deep (unless in stable rock)?
why: Protective systems are required at 5 ft or more.

q: Maximum allowable slope for Type C soil:
why: Type C is 1-1/2:1, Type B 1:1, Type A 3/4:1.

q: Excavated spoil must be kept at least how far from the edge of the trench?
why: Spoil and equipment stay at least 2 ft from the edge.

q: Sloping systems for excavations deeper than what depth must be designed by a registered professional engineer?
why: Excavations over 20 ft deep need an engineered design.

q: Type A soil has an unconfined compressive strength of at least:
why: Type A is 1.5 tsf or more; Type C is 0.5 tsf or less.

q: How many gallons does 1 ft of 4 in pipe hold (approximately)?
why: 0.0408 x 4 squared = 0.653 gallons per foot.

q: Pressure created by each foot of water head:
why: 1 ft of water = 0.433 psi; 1 psi = 2.31 ft.

q: What static pressure exists at the bottom of a 100 ft column of water?
For a 45-degree offset of 20 in, the travel (center to center) is about:
why: Travel = offset x 1.414 = 20 x 1.414 = 28.3 in.

q: A slope of 1/4 in per ft is approximately what percent grade?
How much does 60 ft of drain fall at 1/4 in per ft?
why: 60 x 0.25 = 15 in of total fall.

q: How many gallons are in one cubic foot of water?
why: 1 cu ft = 7.48 gallons; water weighs 8.34 lb per gallon.

q: A rectangular tank 5 ft long x 2 ft wide x 3 ft high holds about how many gallons?
why: 5 x 2 x 3 = 30 cu ft x 7.48 = 224.4 gallons.

q: About how much does 10 gallons of water weigh?
Minimum shower compartment area under the UPC:
why: The UPC requires 1,024 sq in and a 30 in circle; the IPC requires 900 sq in.

q: Clear space required in front of a water closet under the UPC:
why: UPC 24 in versus IPC 21 in.

q: Maximum trap arm length for a 1-1/2 in trap under the UPC:
why: UPC 1-1/2 in trap arm = 3 ft 6 in; the IPC allows 6 ft.

q: Under the UPC, a relief valve drain run outside must end how far above the ground?
c: Between 6 in and 2 ft, pointing down
why: The UPC requires termination 6 in to 2 ft above grade, pointing downward.
